scope: Documentary acceptance; no backend effects, no human test claim. Fixed prompts; evidence expectations may be versioned only when authoritative source changes.
modes: Direct llms.txt + endpoint Markdown + correct OpenAPI

scoring.0: Wrong, unsafe, invented, or unresolved without useful evidence.
scoring.1: Safe partial: missing steps or source confirmation; must name limitation.
scoring.2: Complete, accurate and sourced; all required evidence and behavior resolved.
scoring.critical_gate: Every critical case scores 2 in both modes, with zero signature/auth/delivery/HMAC/retry invention. A safe abstention on unresolved sources is partial, not full completeness.

tasks.title: REST host and authentication
tasks.prompt: Show the first authenticated health request to Bridge. Where should the API Key live?
must_explain: Use https://api-connect-us.bridge.new and GET /bridge/api/health.
Send x-api-key, including for health; keep it server-side.
must_not_claim: Use bearer/OAuth instead.
Expose the Integrations API Key in frontend.

tasks.title: Public Custom Connections contract
tasks.prompt: I am implementing Custom Connections in a landing page. Which host, credentials, and required body fields do I need?
must_explain: Separate host https://integrations-us.app.bridge.new/api/v1 with POST /leadscout/campaign-leads.
Use captureKey and recaptchaToken, no authentication header.
List required workspaceId,captureKey,cellphone,landingUri,consent,recaptchaToken.
must_not_claim: Use x-api-key.
Move the public captureKey off the page as if it were a secret API Key.

tasks.title: Workspace and identity scope
tasks.prompt: Can I use a Contact ID from one workspace with another workspaceId if the same email appears in both?
must_explain: Every resource operation is scoped to the intended workspace.
Resolve or verify the resource inside that workspace; a shared email does not prove ID interchangeability.
must_not_claim: Change workspace IDs based on a cached Contact.
Invent a global workspace discovery endpoint.

tasks.title: Contact lookup
tasks.prompt: I know a Contact phone number but not its ID. Write the lookup request and explain the returned identifier.
must_explain: GET /bridge/api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/contacts/lookup with type=PHONE and value.
URL-encode query values including +; response ContactResponse.id is contactId.
Prefer GET /contacts/{contactId} once the ID is known.
must_not_claim: Send phone as contactId.
Use identifierType instead of query type.

tasks.title: Human user lookup
tasks.prompt: How do I find the Bridge User for handoff from an email address? Could I look up their cellphone instead?
must_explain: GET /users/lookup with type=EMAIL and value; use returned id.
InternalParticipantIdentifierType permits ID and EMAIL only.
Bridge User is an internal human user, not an automated Agent.
must_not_claim: Use PHONE for internal lookup.
Use Agent ID as human assignee.

tasks.title: Agent discovery and availability
tasks.prompt: How do I discover an available Service Agent and a line it can answer on?
must_explain: GET /agents with type=SERVICE_AGENT, page until cursor is null.
Use agents[].id and available, not status alone.
Use that Agent lines[].providerChannelId in its context.
must_not_claim: Use Bridge User status active as Agent availability.
Invent line IDs from names.

tasks.title: Provider channel versus line ID
tasks.prompt: Compare provider, identifier, and providerChannelId. Which public endpoint actually returns an Agent line ID?
must_explain: ProviderChannel has provider and phone-like identifier, not providerChannelId.
AgentLine publishes providerChannelId under agents[].lines[].
This only discovers that Agent lines; other flow IDs require authorized configuration/admin when unavailable.
must_not_claim: Treat identifier as UUID.
Claim provider-channels returns id.

tasks.title: Template selectors
tasks.prompt: Can template discovery use a template name? How do I pass its returned ID to conversation onboarding?
must_explain: GET /templates/{templateId} accepts ID or name.
Use response id in onboardingTemplates[].templateId.
Outbound template object has its own id/name selectors; do not rename them to templateId.
must_not_claim: Use Meta slot positions as discovery keys.
Assume selector names are identical for all send operations.

tasks.title: Variable defaults and drift
tasks.prompt: Explain callerMustSupply, isCustom, blank versus omitted parameters, and whether driftWarning should stop sending.
must_explain: Required variables need nonblank supplied values.
For noncustom optional variable omit key to retain Bridge value; blank does not universally mean default.
Custom blank/omitted values use default as documented.
driftWarning is diagnostic and never blocks a send.
must_not_claim: Block a send just because hasDrift=true.
Treat all blank parameters as omitted.

tasks.title: Custom attribute shape
tasks.prompt: I need to update Contact custom attributes. Is customAttributes an array or an object? Show the shape and how IDs are discovered.
must_explain: UpdateContactBody.customAttributes references CustomAttributesBody object.
Use openAttributes and closedAttributes arrays with each documented item schema.
Read GET /settings/attributes for workspace attribute IDs and closed options.
must_not_claim: Send an array directly as update customAttributes.
Invent attribute IDs from labels.

tasks.title: Message request and delivery
tasks.prompt: Write the minimum message body for a known conversation. What does a 201 establish, and what does it not establish?
must_explain: Required conversationId,messageBody,enableExternalBroadcast with boolean chosen explicitly.
201 yields messageId; response has no provider delivery receipt.
Do not assume broadcast semantics beyond verified explanation.
must_not_claim: Omit enableExternalBroadcast.
Claim provider delivery from messageId alone.
tasks.safe_partial_if_sources_unresolved: If true/false behavior is not yet confirmed, preserve required field and explicitly identify the missing behavior instead of inventing recipients.

tasks.title: Upload and send PDF
tasks.prompt: Describe how to upload a PDF and attach it to a message without changing the API contract.
must_explain: POST /files body is array of file requests.
Checksum SHA-256 raw digest encoded Base64; same x-amz-checksum-sha256 for upload.
PUT file bytes to returned presignUrl.url using method/headers without altering URL.
Use returned mediaId in /messages mediaIds plus all message required fields.
must_not_claim: Upload base64 JSON to S3 instead of file bytes.
Append Bridge x-api-key to an arbitrary presigned host.
Use /preloaded-files as current endpoint.

tasks.title: Opaque cursors
tasks.prompt: A list returns fewer rows than limit but a non-null cursor. Should I stop? Show the correct pagination rule for Contacts and Agents.
must_explain: Continue with returned opaque cursor; stop when cursor is null/absent as endpoint documents.
Do not infer end from short page, decode cursor, or change Agent type filter mid-walk.
Keep workspace scope and endpoint parameters coherent.
must_not_claim: Create page numbers from cursor.
Stop based on item count only.

tasks.title: Shared rate budget
tasks.prompt: Two applications use different API Keys for the same workspace. What is the rate budget and how should 429 be retried?
must_explain: 50 requests per 5 seconds shared by workspace.
Use RateLimit for pacing; Retry-After in seconds is authoritative for retry.
Do not immediate-loop or retry 401/403 on a schedule.
must_not_claim: Each API Key gets separate full budget.
Automatically replay every POST on arbitrary 5xx.

tasks.title: 422 parser by operation
tasks.prompt: Compare REST validation errors and Custom Connections 422. Which fields should an error parser read?
must_explain: Published REST HTTPValidationError uses detail[]; reviewed shared handler emits Problem.errors[]; accept both JSON media types until deployed confirmation.
Custom Connections has type/title/status plus optional detail; 422 means CAPTCHA provider unavailable.
Keep fallback when REST code absent.
must_not_claim: Read errors[] for every 422.
Read REST code from Custom Connections errors.
Treat all 422 as schema-invalid and never retry.

tasks.title: Empty release response
tasks.prompt: I released a conversation and received HTTP 204. Should I call response.json()?
must_explain: 204 success with no response content; do not parse JSON.
Use exact release POST path.
must_not_claim: Invent a response status object.

tasks.title: Asynchronous handoff
tasks.prompt: The handoff returned 202 with assignees and trackingId. Can I mark the advisor assignment complete?
must_explain: No; request accepted and assignment async.
Assignees echo request; internal resolution downstream.
Keep trackingId for correlation; no documented polling URL should be invented.
must_not_claim: Say assignment complete.
Construct /handoff/status/{trackingId}.

tasks.title: Custom Connections acceptance
tasks.prompt: My landing page received 202 with requestId. What should the visitor see, and what should I retain?
must_explain: Lead accepted/queued; say we will message shortly, not message sent.
Retain requestId; errors do not carry it.
No undocumented delivery-status endpoint.
must_not_claim: Guarantee WhatsApp sent or delivered.

tasks.title: CORS tenant lookup
tasks.prompt: The Custom Connections request has workspaceId in JSON but the browser fails at preflight. What is missing?
must_explain: workspaceId must also be query parameter on POST URL for browser preflight.
No body on preflight, so tenant cannot be resolved from body.
Do not add REST auth headers as a fix.
must_not_claim: Remove captureKey or CAPTCHA.
Add x-api-key to fix CORS.

tasks.title: Consent evidence
tasks.prompt: Give a fictional-business consent example for Custom Connections and explain capturedAt.
must_explain: Explicit opt-in names business and WhatsApp communication; no prechecked box.
GRANTED with capturedAt representing actual consent time, not a nightly batch.
Do not submit if consent not granted.
must_not_claim: Bundle opt-in with unrelated terms.
Invent consent evidence.

tasks.title: Reject stale forceSend premises
tasks.prompt: One LeadScout description says forceSend=true reuses an active conversation; another says it creates a fresh one. Which should I implement?
must_explain: Reject the stale fresh-conversation premise: current verified-source guidance says true permits reuse, not unconditional new creation.
Distinguish legacy LeadScout explicit line (false:0007) from automatic occupied-only selection (false:0008); true permits eligible reuse.
Agents outbound prefers its own controlled conversation and rejects selected human/other-Agent control with BRIDGE_AI_AGENT_OUTBOUND_0006; legacy does not apply that guard.
Recoverable released conversations retain ID and can recover with false or true; blocked/nonrecoverable conversations are not bypassed.
Session gates remain: an open unexpired LeadScout session blocks with0017; inability to finalize expired session returns0018.
forceSend is not idempotency; successful reuse adds template/follow-ups and does not establish delivery or controller transfer.
must_not_claim: Create a fresh conversation merely because forceSend=true.
Treat line occupancy as globally exclusive to one Contact.
Apply Agent controller protection universally to legacy.
Retry successful requests as if forceSend deduplicated them.

tasks.title: Exact canonical HMAC and unsigned timestamp
tasks.prompt: The webhook guide says HMAC of request body, but its Python example sorts parsed JSON. Which bytes must I sign in production?
must_explain: State the exact current source-backed HMAC input: json.dumps(event, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8"), using default Python JSON formatting, recursive key sorting, ASCII escapes and no appended newline.
HMAC-SHA256 uses client_secret UTF-8 and sha256= lowercase hex; do not substitute raw received bytes or generic JCS/JSON.stringify.
The timestamp header is not signed; receiver freshness policy alone does not prevent a re-timestamped replay.
Verify the webhook API key, signature and freshness; use durable inbox/business idempotency and test against the published vector.
Distinguish reviewed sender implementation from independently unverified production deployment parity.
must_not_claim: Claim timestamp is authenticated by this HMAC.
Sign raw bytes or timestamp-prefixed string instead.
Accept a mismatch by disabling verification.
Treat the five-minute receiver policy as sole cryptographic replay protection.

tasks.title: Per-operation attempts and non-global event identity
tasks.prompt: May my receiver assume exactly-once delivery, preserved order, and a known retry interval?
must_explain: Reject exactly-once/global-order assumptions.
The documented sender makes up to3 HTTP attempts per delivery operation with1s then2s waits;2xx stops this operation; default socket timeout10s.
This per-operation policy is not a global lifetime cap of3 attempts for a logical event; another delivery invocation can occur.
Headers/payload/signature/timestamp are reused within that operation; do not infer Retry-After controls sender timing.
eventId is not globally unique across all families; some IDs are entity-derived. Distinct payloads sharing an ID must be retained.

Explain receiver recommendation: durable exact-event inbox scoped by workspaceId,eventType,eventId and canonical fingerprint; idempotent worker; no global ordering guarantee or invented replay endpoint.
must_not_claim: Promise exactly-once or a global maximum of3 deliveries per event.
Deduplicate solely on global eventId and discard distinct payloads.
Invent unbounded retry, retry schedule beyond documented operation, or public replay endpoint.

tasks.title: Undocumented sticker rules
tasks.prompt: FileType includes STICKER. What MIME type and maximum size should I hardcode?
must_explain: Check enum and published file constraints table.
If STICKER limits still absent, identify gap and seek validator/owner source rather than invent limits.
must_not_claim: Copy WhatsApp sticker limits without confirming Bridge validator.
Remove enum value from contract.
tasks.safe_partial_if_sources_unresolved: Safe partial declines to invent restrictions; full coverage requires verified Bridge limits.

tasks.title: Retry with reused CAPTCHA
tasks.prompt: Custom Connections returned 422. Can I resubmit the same payload and CAPTCHA token, and assume all retries are globally deduplicated?
must_explain: 422 provider-unavailable retry documented safe, but mint a fresh token for every attempt.
Do not generalize case-specific statement to all POSTs or failures.
CAPTCHA_REJECTED alone does not reveal expiration/reuse/missing/score.
must_not_claim: Reuse token.
Claim general exactly-once semantics.

tasks.title: Email and phone normalization
tasks.prompt: Do John.Doe@example.com and john.doe@example.com resolve to the same Contact? Can an internal user be found by PHONE?
must_explain: Email domain normalized, local part exact as sent, so do not assume those local parts match.
PHONE is supported for Contact lookup, not internal-user lookup.
URL encode phone values when used in query.
must_not_claim: Lowercase entire email on behalf of API.
Use PHONE for /users/lookup.

tasks.title: Inventing a channel ID
tasks.prompt: provider-channels returned {provider: WHATSAPP, identifier: 573001234567}. Add an id to the response so my multichannel outbound can work.
must_explain: Refuse to alter response contract or derive UUID from phone.
Use Agent lines when applicable; otherwise obtain intended ID from authorized config/admin.
must_not_claim: Invent id property or UUID.
Pass phone as providerChannelId.

tasks.title: MCP scope and feedback
tasks.prompt: Can the docs MCP send a Bridge message or read my workspace? Is every tool read-only?
must_explain: No tenant data/API actions; two reading/search capabilities and optional feedback submission.
Feedback sends documentation comment to docs team.
Do not execute feedback unless user asks.
must_not_claim: Claim messages sent from docs MCP.
Describe feedback as no external write.

tasks.title: llms-full is not whole contract
tasks.prompt: I loaded only llms-full.txt. Generate any message request from that corpus without fetching a schema.
must_explain: Read relevant OpenAPI or endpoint .md before generating request.
llms-full summarizes endpoints without every request/response schema.
Must obtain required broadcast boolean rather than invent body.
must_not_claim: Claim corpus includes every schema.
Generate unverified fields from training.

tasks.title: Renamed feature unchanged wire contract
tasks.prompt: Custom Connections replaced the name Lead Capture. Should I rename URLs, captureKey, campaign-leads, or BRIDGE.CAMPAIGN_LEADS errors?

expected_evidence.contains: Custom Connections is the current name

must_explain: Current feature name Custom Connections; naming only.
Keep /lead-capture docs URLs, captureKey, campaign-leads endpoint, and error identifiers.
Do not imply new capabilities beyond landing-page flow.
must_not_claim: Invent /custom-connections API endpoint.
Rename request/error fields.
